title: Example QA Review: Skeptic Perspective
body:
# Example QA Review: Skeptic Perspective

This worked example shows a `qa-skeptic` `review_report.json` aligned to the current schema. It demonstrates how to classify issues by `block`, `revise`, and `note`, and how to issue a `REVISE` gate decision for a fixable section.

---

## Source Document Excerpt

*Section 3: Choosing the Right Approach for Your Stage*

> ML recommendation systems have been shown to significantly improve user engagement across a wide range of applications. Many companies that have adopted these systems report impressive results, with some seeing engagement increases of up to 40% or more. The technology has matured considerably in recent years, making it more accessible to companies of all sizes.
>
> For early-stage products, it is generally advisable to start simple and add complexity as your needs grow. A basic recommendation approach can be implemented relatively quickly with modern tools and libraries. Teams should consider their specific context when making this decision.
>
> The most important factor is having clean data. Without good data, even the most sophisticated algorithm will produce poor results. Organizations that invest in data quality early tend to see better outcomes from their recommendation systems over time.

---

## QA Review Output - Skeptic Perspective

```json
{
  "review_id": "REV-SKEPTIC-001",
  "draft_ref": "artifacts/drafts/draft-001.md",
  "brief_id": "BRIEF-001",
  "run_id": "RUN-001",
  "perspectives_applied": ["skeptic"],
  "issues": [
    {
      "issue_id": "SKEPTIC-001",
      "perspective": "skeptic",
      "severity": "block",
      "location": "Section 3, paragraph 1",
      "description": "The opening paragraph makes several performance claims without grounding, including an undefined engagement increase range.",
      "suggested_fix": "Remove the unsupported claims or replace them with sourced evidence tied to the brief's scope."
    },
    {
      "issue_id": "SKEPTIC-002",
      "perspective": "skeptic",
      "severity": "revise",
      "location": "Section 3, paragraph 2",
      "description": "The guidance is vague and does not provide the stage-based decision signal promised by the outline.",
      "suggested_fix": "Rewrite the paragraph around explicit decision criteria for early-stage products."
    },
    {
      "issue_id": "SKEPTIC-003",
      "perspective": "skeptic",
      "severity": "note",
      "location": "Section 3, paragraph 3",
      "description": "The clean-data point is useful but would land better with one specific mechanism instead of a generic closing generalization.",
      "suggested_fix": "Keep the claim and add one concrete example of how dirty data harms recommendation quality."
    }
  ],
  "gate_decision": "REVISE",
  "gate_justification": "The section is fixable without new research, but it cannot advance until the unsupported claims are removed and the decision guidance is made concrete.",
  "blocking_issues_count": 1,
  "revise_issues_count": 1,
  "created_by": "qa-skeptic",
  "created_at": "2026-03-31T09:00:00Z"
}
```

---

## Annotation: Gate Decisions

**BLOCK:** The section cannot be made acceptable through ordinary revision because core structure, source support, or canon alignment is broken.

**REVISE (this example):** The section is directionally correct but cannot advance until the listed issues are fixed.

**ACCEPT:** The section can advance. Notes may remain, but no blocking or required-revision issues remain.
